sections.text:
This horse-like creature appears demon-possessed: eyes glowing a hellish red, muscles unnaturally swollen with such power that they threaten to tear its skin, hooves ripping up the ground as it rampages. A twisted, crimson lance of carriage and scar tissue gram from the stump of its horn, a grizzly parody of the pearly lance carried by a normal unicorn. Thin lines of blood run down its face and into its mane. The creature seems to be emitting one constant scream of insanity, interrupted by the occasional gasping breath

Fiendish Presence (Su) A bloodlance is forever plagued by disembodied chaotic evil outsiders. Protection from evil and protection from chaos hedge out these forces; for the duration, the bloodlance loses its magic circle and spell-like abilities. A bloodlance so affected acts naturally: it does not regain its sanity or attempt to communicate.

Because of their unique magical properties, unicorn horns are a coveted commodity among evil alchemists and spellcasters, most of whom are not above hunting down a living unicorn to get one. While most at least have the decency to kill the noble creature before taking its horn, the most twisted among them are sadistic enough to simply saw off the horn of a living unicorn, leaving the creature in unending, unspeakable pain. The evilest rituals even require the unicorn remain among the living. While many of these poor creatures spend the rest of their short lives in crippling misery, some are fated to worse: they first go mad, then fail under demonic influence, becoming hellish perversions of their kind.

The noble kirin roam the sky, their feet rarely touching soil. They have a stag’s graceful body and cloven hooves, a pair of backward-facing horns, and a thick mane and tail ranging from golden to brilliant reds or purples in the hues of the setting sun. Their hide resembles that of a dragon, the scales gleaming ebon or iridescent green. Rare in the extreme, kirin seldom meddle openly in worldly affairs, preferring a subtle hand in overturning the schemes of wicked spirits such as hags and oni. The blood of young kirin runs hot, however, and such spirited youths may serve as mounts for cavaliers and paladins of clever wit and untarnished moral quality.

sections.heading: Unicorn, Hornsaw
sections.text:
The Hornsaw unicorn resembles nothing more than a shaggy war horse with a serrated horn, wicked cloven hooves and unusually pointed teeth. It's omnivorous,
and although it's usually content to graze, it will gladly eat the bodies of intruders in its domain. It rarely hunts for food or sport, but it can be remarkably aggressive when defending its territory. These beasts possess an unusual level of cunning, and most have learned to understand several languages appropriate to their surroundings (although they cannot speak).

Unicorn

Unicorns are fierce, intelligent creatures of the forest, noble beasts who keep their own counsel and typically appear only to defend their homes against evil. They universally shun all creatures except for good-aligned fey, good-aligned humanoid women, and the woodlands' native animals, though they may fight alongside other good creatures against common enemies.

Frequency rare

Organization solitary, mated pair, or curse (3–6)

Unicorns generally make their homes in specific glades or dells within the vast forests they protect (these regions can cover anywhere from a few dozen square miles to hundreds). They allow good and neutral creatures to pass through, hunt for food, or reside in their woods unharmed, but evil creatures and those who damage the local ecosystem more than necessary through sport hunting or commercial logging are swiftly driven out or killed.

On rare occasions, lone unicorns of Large size (CR 6), without mates or whose partners have been slain, have been known to adopt young women of exceptionally pure virtue as surrogates, allowing the women to ride on their backs and becoming their guardians and protectors. This bond generally ends if the woman becomes more committed to someone else—such as a lover or child.

A unicorn's horn is the focus for its powers, and in order to use its spell-like abilities on other creatures the unicorn must touch them with it. Evil creatures greatly value unicorn horns as reagents for healing potions and other dark rites, and a single powdered unicorn horn counts as 1,600 gp when used as a component for crafting healing magic.

For a riding unicorn, apply the Giant simple template.

Unicorns expand their repertoire of racial spell-like abilities as they gain racial Hit Dice. A specimen with all of the abilities in the Pathfinder Bestiary would have 10 HD (with access to 5th level spell-like abilities; +1 to Cha upon reaching 8 HD) and be CR 6. Alicorns are as evil as unicorns are good, using their razor-sharp horns and claw-like hooves as weapons. They attack any weaker creatures for the sheer pleasure of killing, but will try to avoid stronger parties.

Because of their unique magical properties, unicorn horns are a coveted commodity among evil alchemists and spellcasters, most of whom are not above hunting down a living unicorn to get one. The noble kirin roam the sky, their feet rarely touching soil. They have a stag’s graceful body and cloven hooves, a pair of backward-facing horns, and a thick mane and tail ranging from golden to brilliant reds or purples in the hues of the setting sun. Their hide resembles that of a dragon, the scales gleaming ebon or iridescent green. Rare in the extreme, kirin seldom meddle openly in worldly affairs, preferring a subtle hand in overturning the schemes of wicked spirits such as hags and oni. The blood of young kirin runs hot, however, and such spirited youths may serve as mounts for cavaliers and paladins of clever wit and untarnished moral quality.

sections.heading: Ursikka
sections.text:
This insect-like creature is covered in downy white fur. A pair of eyes gleams above a three-part mouth that drips viscous fluid. Held aloft by four slender legs, on which they skitter with unsettling speed, ursikka can reach heights of 25 feet, with a long, lean abdomen accounting for most of their 20-foot length. Their grasping forearms each end in a sharp pincer capable of shearing flesh from bone, and shaggy fur covers the majority of their bodies. The ursikka's most unusual trait, however, is a three-part maw that can open wide enough to swallow humans whole. Freezing saliva drips constantly from these gnashing mandibles, injuring and trapping prey.
UrsikkaPB5	Cr 9
Giant (x2), monstrousSS, vermin animal paragon 2
N Huge magical beast [augmented vermin]
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent, tremorsense 60 ft.; Perception +15
AC 25, touch 12, flat-footed 21
(-2 size, +4 dodge, +13 natural)
hp 138 (12 HD; LW 69/HW 34); Diehard
Immune cold, [mind-affecting]

Melee bite +19 (2d6+9 plus poison) and
2 claws +14 (2d6+4 plus grab)
Face 10 ft. x 20 ft.; Reach 10 ft.

Special Atks poison (freezing saliva: bite, spit, or grapple—contact DC 22, 5d6 cold/rd. plus entangled 1 rd. for 12 rounds; cure 2 saves, DC 19 Str check, or 15 hp fire damage)
Attributes Str 28, Dex 10, Con 22, Int 2, Wis 13,  Cha 5
SQ hibernation
Feats Additional Traits, Dodge, Improved Natural Armor, Improved Grapple, Improved Initiative, Skirmish
Skills Athletics (1/+13), Endurance (12/+21), Perception (11/+15)
Environment any cold land
Frequency rare
Organization solitary, pair, or hive (3-10)
Freezing Saliva (Su) Ray of frost (0 level) + Cascade Spell [(bind; +1 level) + Extend Spell (1 rd./level to 1 rd.; -1 level)] + Extend Spell (onset: inst. to 1 rd./level; +2 levels) + Tenuous Spell (-1 level) + Bouncing Spell (+1 level) + Channel Spell (+1 level) + Restricted Spell (immune to cold; -1 level) = 2nd level; damage cap 5d6 cold/rd. plus entangled 1 rd. for 1 rd./level or until make 2 saves.

Hibernation (Ex) An ursikka can enter a prolonged state of hibernation by surrounding itself with its spittle, which hardens into a cocoon. While hibernating, an ursikka doesn't need to drink or eat. The cocoon has hardness 10, 60 hp, and is immune to fire damage. As long as the cocoon remains intact, the ursikka remains unharmed in its hibernation. An ursikka must use its attacks to break free from its cocoon.
Ursikka are vicious apex predators that rule vast arctic territories. With only a bestial intellect, ursikka view all smaller creatures as food, and think nothing of invading and devouring entire humanoid communities.
During summers, ursikka live inside cocoons constructed from their own saliva, impenetrable sheathes that protect ursikka from the brutal summer heat. Shortly after their spittle-cocoons harden, the beasts go dormant and do not awake until the temperature returns to a more tolerable level. An ursikka that is interrupted while weaving its cocoon immediately attempts to kill the intruders. An ursikka whose cocoon is broken during the summer emerges similarly enraged

sections.heading: Wakandagi
sections.text:
This is the name of a water monster in the traditions and beliefs of the Omaha and Mohawk Native American people of the United States. This massive being has a long serpentine body with horns on its head and legs with hooves, all of which resemble those of a deer. However, it is observed only infrequently and even then only through a mist, but it will attract and dispose of anyone who is foolish enough to travel in this region alone. The wakandagi was said to inhabit vast lakes and stretches of the Missouri River, where it would challenge those who ventured on its waters by throwing spheres of water at them.
―Carol Rose, Giants, Monsters & Dragons: An Encyclopedia of Folklore, Legend, and Myth (2000)

sections.heading: Lamhigyn
sections.text:
This small, three-eyed creature has ragged, red-streaked wings and a menacingly barbed tail. Llamhigyns y Dwr (“water leapers”) are strange-looking creatures often characterized by mortals visiting the Abyss as overgrown, flying tadpoles with bat wings and stinger-tipped tails. Their bulbous, unblinking eyes are vaguely froglike, and are often the last things unprepared adventurers see, as the pesky creatures are fond of wrapping their wings around their victims’ heads to blind their prey. Their tiny mouths house thick tongues that flick about in the presence of prey. Llamhigyns have thick, scaly skin ranging in color from red to green. Though llamhigyns are typically encountered flying, on the ground they stand on four insectile legs that they keep tucked beneath them while nesting. Although they are small, their 2-foot-high, 8-pound bodies are impressive sights when hurtling through the air at their victims.

Elite animal paragon 3
CE Small outsider [demon]
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +8
Languages Abyssal

(+1 size, +2 Dex, +3 natural)
hp 32 (5 HD; LW 16/HW 8)

2 wings +3 (1d3+2 plus grab)

Feats Blinding Strike, Feat Mastery (blinding strike), Improved Initiative
Skills Athletics (0/+4; swim +8), Fly (5/+11), Perception (4/+8), Stealth (1/+10)
Environment any aquatic (Abyss)
Frequency uncommon
Organization solitary, clutch (2–9), or hive (10–30)
Treasure none

Llamhigyns are simple pests that emerged from the chaotic fabric of the Abyss. They poison their prey until it falls into a coma, and then they slowly tear it apart, piece by piece, with their rasping mouths. Llamhigyns view intruders on their territory with disdain, and their stings have left many adventurers insane and debilitated, opportune victims for the Abyss’s insatiable predators. Though llamhigyns might not appear frightening on their own, greater terrors sometimes follow in their wakes, hoping for easy meals.
When it comes to their own kind, llamhigyns can be quite volatile. In general, they tend to get along with other llamhigyns, though almost anything can set them off. When this happens, llamhigyns unleash the full force of their chaotic fury on each other, stinging and grappling until only one—or sometimes none—of the bizarre creatures remain.
When they’re not fighting among themselves, llamhigyns live together in noisy, flapping hives, waiting for hapless creatures to stumble into their dens. When it comes to victims, llamhigyns prefer those that can think and walk, for they provide the most deliciously terrified reactions. There is nothing llamhigyns love more than injecting their mind-numbing toxin into terrified victims while they ineffectually scream and flail. Llamhigyns ignore most normal animals unless they have waited too long for fresh prey and have grown bored. Sometimes, however, a particularly large hive of llamhigyns will attempt to bring down large, imposing creatures simply for the challenge of it.

sections.heading: Wemic
sections.text:
There were these beings, maybe two dozen of them, and I've never seen anyone or anything run so fast. They had four legs and from the waist down appeared to be feline, smaller than the dzur, perhaps the size of the tiassa but without wings. From the waist up they appeared human. They carried spears.
"Cat-centaurs, Loiosh?"
"I guess so, boss. I hadn't known they were real."
―Steven Brust, Taltos (19)
Wemics have the body of a lion with a humanoid torso extending from what would be the lion’s neck. From head to rump, they are 10 to12 feet long, while they are 6 to 7 feet tall when standing erect. Their entire bodies are covered in dusky golden fur, and the tail is tipped with a brush of black hair. Adult males have a mane of long black hair that covers the top and back of the head and extends down to the neck and shoulders. Their underbellies are white. A wemic’s face is a mixture of human and leonine features, with a black or russet nose, gold eyes with catlike pupils, and high-set ears. All six limbs end in claws; the claws on the humanoid arms and leonine forelimbs are retractable.

They had four legs and from the waist down appeared to be feline, smaller than the dzur, perhaps the size of the tiassa but without wings. From the waist up they appeared human. They carried spears.

"Cat-centaurs, Loiosh?"

"I guess so, boss. I hadn't known they were real."

―Steven Brust, Taltos (19)

Wemics have the body of a lion with a humanoid torso extending from what would be the lion’s neck. From head to rump, they are 10 to12 feet long, while they are 6 to 7 feet tall when standing erect. Their entire bodies are covered in dusky golden fur, and the tail is tipped with a brush of black hair. Adult males have a mane of long black hair that covers the top and back of the head and extends down to the neck and shoulders. Their underbellies are white. A wemic’s face is a mixture of human and leonine features, with a black or russet nose, gold eyes with catlike pupils, and high-set ears. All six limbs end in claws; the claws on the humanoid arms and leonine forelimbs are retractable.

sections.heading: Wharlysk
sections.text:
The semi-reptilian wharlysk lurks deep in the hearts of particularly moist jungles, often near rivers, where it uses its mastery over sound to capture prey. A wharlysk's head combines the worst aspects of a warthog's and a viper's, down to the razor-sharp tusks and the forked tongue. It has a long, powerful neck attached to a newt-like body, and a single row of six long tentacles tipped with scorpion-like pinchers writhe down the length of its striped back. The wharlysk's skin is always slimy, and its six legs end in powerful webbed feet armed with sharp claws to aid in climbs through the canopy above, when it can find trees large enough to support its weight. A wharlysk is usually about 25 feet long, but it coils up on itself when in combat.

sections.heading: Woozy
sections.text:
The creature was all squares and flat surfaces and edges. Its head was an exact square, like one of the building-blocks103 a child plays with; therefore it had no ears, but heard sounds through two openings in the upper corners. Its nose, being in the center of a square surface, was flat, while the mouth was formed by the opening of the lower edge of the block. The body of the Woozy was much larger than its head, but was likewise block-shaped—being twice as long as it was wide and high. The tail was square and stubby and perfectly straight, and the four legs were made in the same way, each being four-sided. The animal was covered with a thick, smooth skin and had no hair at all except at the extreme end of its tail, where there grew exactly three stiff, stubby hairs. The beast was dark blue in color and his face was not fierce nor ferocious in expression, but rather good-humored and droll.
―L. Frank Baum, The Patchwork Girl of Oz (1913)

The woozy (a nonesuch) is much hated by Munchkin farmers due to its preference for eating honeybees, and much feared due to its terrifying roar and tendency to spark actual fire from its eyes when angered. When local farmers found their weapons and implements could not penetrate its hide, they penned it behind a high fence. Despite its fearsome reputation, however, the Woozy is an amiable, shy, honest, and generally agreeable creature.

sections.heading: Ooze
sections.text:
Oozes share some common characteristics, regardless of their size:
Languages: None.
Attributes Modifiers: Oozes use the following default racial attribute array: Str 15, Dex 1, Con 18, Int —, Wis 1, Cha 1. Being mindless, they are immune to [mind-affecting] spells and effects. Although they have no intelligence score, like constructs they still gain feats and skills as appropriate for their Hit Dice. Typical skills include Athletics, Endurance, and/or Perception. Typical feats include Improved Grapple, Improved Initiative, Improved Overrun, Toughness, and Vital Strike (to constrict a grappled opponent).
Racial Feats: Oozes have the following racial feats in common:
Amorphous (Ex): The ooze’s lack of a definite anatomy rovides immunity to flanking and to precision damage and effects, including critical hits, sneak attacks, and most [Strike] feats). Primitive Organism (Ex): Oozes are immune to paralysis, poison, sleep, and stunning. They do not suffer wound penalties due to loss of hp.
Racial Traits: Oozes have the following traits in common:
Blind: An ooze is immune to visual effects, gaze attacks, illusions, and other attack forms that rely on sight. They cannot gain darkvision or low-light vision.Blindsight (Ex): The ooze’s entire body is a sense organ, providing blindsight 60 ft.Slow: An ooze’s base speed is 20 ft.Oozes also gain one additional trait, usually agile climber (climb speed equal to land speed), feat mastery (grapple), strong swimmer (swim speed equal to land speed), etc.
Weapon Familiarity: Oozes use a slam as a primary natural attack (base damage 1d6 for a Medium ooze). They are not proficient with weapons or armor of any kind.
Racial Progression: Oozes typically have levels in “ooze creature” (see below), a PC class. They can also progress by racial Hit Dice (d8, BAB medium, 2 skill points/HD; +1 CR per 3 racial HD).

Ooze Creature	Hit Dice: d8
Level | Base Atk | Special Abilities
1st | +0 | Acid, adaptation, attribute boost, weakness (optional)
2nd | +1 | Adaptation, attribute boost
3rd | +2 | Adaptation, attribute boost
4th | +3 | Adaptation, attribute boost
5th | +3 | Adaptation, attribute boost

Saving Throws: Ooze creatures do not gain a class bonus to saving throws.
Class Skills: Ooze creatures have no class skills.
Skill Points at Each Level: 2 + Int modifier.
Acid (Ex): Ooze creatures deal acid damage on a successful grapple or slam attack (base 1d6 damage for a Medium ooze creature). Instead of acid, some oozes gain Improved Natural Attack with their slam.
Attribute Boost (Ex): Ooze creature levels do not provide the elite attribute array. Rather, each class level provides a +2 racial bonus to any one attribute score. These stack with existing racial bonuses, and with each other (if more than one such bonus is applied to the same attribute).
Adaptation (Ex): Oozes are simple protoplasmic beings with a bewildering number of special adaptations. At each class level, an ooze creature gains one such adaptation. Some of the more common ones are listed here; others can be included.
Constrict (Ex): The ooze gains Improved Grapple and Vital Strike as bonus feats. If its base attack bonus is less than +6, it also gains Feat Mastery (Grapple).Corrosive Acid (Ex): Weapons striking the ooze take acid damage as if the ooze creature had struck them, unless the wielder succeeds at a Reflex save (DC 10 + half the ooze’s racial HD + the ooze’s Constitution modifier). When the ooze constricts an opponent, the target’s clothing and armor are also potentially affected by the ooze’s acid (Reflex save at DC 14 + half the ooze’s racial HD + the ooze’s Con modifier negates the effect for that round).Damage Reduction (Ex): The ooze creature gains DR 5/— (10/— if HD 12+).Engulf (Ex): The ooze gains Improved Overrun, Skirmish, and Throat Punch as bonus feats.Gaseous Form (Ex): The ooze exists as a cloud of smoke or vapor. It loses its Strength score and slam attack, and cannot wear or wield items. However, it gains a Fly speed of 20 ft., damage reduction 10/magic, immunity to poison, and can pass through tiny openings (anything not airtight). For purposes of Fly checks and wind effects, its size is treated as if it were 4 categories smaller than actual (minimum Fine). Immunities (Ex): Select two of the following: acid, bludgeoning damage, cold, electricity, fire, force, negative energy, piercing damage, slashing damage, or sonic. This adaptation can be selected multiple times; each time, choose two more immunities.Natural Armor (Ex): The ooze secretes a shell or hard coating that provides it with a natural armor bonus equal to its ooze creature level, +/-3 per size category above or below Medium.Poison (Ex): The ooze secretes an anesthetizing slime; treat as contact poison; 1d2 Dex/round for 6 rounds, cure 1 save. Some oozes secrete a weakening poison instead (Str damage instead of Dex).Quicksilver (Ex): The ooze flows like liquid mercury; it gains a +10 racial bonus to its Dexterity score (generally increasing it to 11).Split (Ex): Choose two damage types. When the ooze takes damage of that type (or is struck by an attack dealing that type of damage, if immune), it splits into two identical copies of itself (apply damage first, if applicable). Each copy has half the original's remaining hit points (rounded down). An ooze with 10 or fewer hp cannot be further split, and can be killed normally.Suction (Ex): The ooze can create powerful suction against any surface as it climbs, allowing it to cling to inverted surfaces with ease (as the spider climb spell). It can establish or release suction as a swift action; as long as it is using suction, it moves at half speed. Because of the suction, the ooze’s CMD score gets a +10 circumstance bonus to resist bull rush and other attacks and effects that attempt to physically move it from its location.Transparent (Ex): Due to its lack of vivid coloration, the ooze is difficult to discern from its surroundings in most environments. A Perception check (DC 20 + the monster’s Stealth bonus) is required to notice the ooze. Any creature that fails to notice the ooze and walks into it automatically suffers damage as if struck by the ooze's slam attack and is immediately subject to a grab attempt (if applicable) by the ooze.
Weakness (Ex): An ooze can gain a weakness (typical vulnerability to a common energy type). In exchange, it gains one immunity (see above). If an ooze gains fire immunity and vulnerability to cold, it can also gain the [fire] subtype and change its acid to additional fire damage. Other combinations (cold, etc.) are also possible.

sections.text:

Ooze creature 4

Attributes Str 16, Dex 1, Con 26, Int —, Wis 1, Cha 1

Feats Improved Grapple, Improved OverrunB, SkirmishB, Throat PunchB, Vital Strike
Skills Stealth (4/-5)

Frequency uncommon
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

One of the dungeon's most unusual and specialized predators, gelatinous cubes spend their existence mindlessly roaming dungeon halls and dark caverns, swallowing up organic material such as plants, refuse, carrion, and even living creatures. Materials the cube cannot digest, such as metal and stone, can eventually fill up the creature's mass with such detritus, and at times the creature may excrete some of this material out of its body. Often the treasure and possessions of past victims remain inside the gelatinous cube, leaving a ghostly impression of their material remains.
Sages believe these creatures evolved as a specialized advancement of gray oozes. Some beings use gelatinous cubes as protectors of dungeons and underground fortifications, trapping the immense creatures in massive metal crates and transporting them through either slave power or magic to their final guard posts. They make particularly efficient waste disposals as well—a tribe that can trap a gelatinous cube in a pit or other area that it cannot climb out of can use it as a midden or even a deadly trap, depending only on the ingenuity of the creatures who caught it.
In locations with plentiful sources of food, gelatinous cubes can exist for hundreds of years, if not thousands. However, if denied organic material for more than 6 months, a gelatinous cube begins shrinking. Eventually this stresses its walls and the creature leaks rapidly evaporating slimy liquid until its body collapses and disappears completely.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: standard; trait: feat mastery (overrun); adaptations: engulf, immunities, poison, transparent.

Level

Base Atk

Special Abilities

1st

2nd

Adaptation, attribute boost

Saving Throws: Ooze creatures do not gain a class bonus to saving throws.

Class Skills: Ooze creatures have no class skills.

Skill Points at Each Level: 2 + Int modifier.

Acid (Ex): Ooze creatures deal acid damage on a successful grapple or slam attack (base 1d6 damage for a Medium ooze creature). Instead of acid, some oozes gain Improved Natural Attack with their slam.

Attribute Boost (Ex): Ooze creature levels do not provide the elite attribute array. Rather, each class level provides a +2 racial bonus to any one attribute score. These stack with existing racial bonuses, and with each other (if more than one such bonus is applied to the same attribute).

Adaptation (Ex): Oozes are simple protoplasmic beings with a bewildering number of special adaptations. At each class level, an ooze creature gains one such adaptation. Some of the more common ones are listed here; others can be included.

  • Constrict (Ex): The ooze gains Improved Grapple and Vital Strike as bonus feats. If its base attack bonus is less than +6, it also gains Feat Mastery (Grapple).
  • Corrosive Acid (Ex): Weapons striking the ooze take acid damage as if the ooze creature had struck them, unless the wielder succeeds at a Reflex save (DC 10 + half the ooze’s racial HD + the ooze’s Constitution modifier). When the ooze constricts an opponent, the target’s clothing and armor are also potentially affected by the ooze’s acid (Reflex save at DC 14 + half the ooze’s racial HD + the ooze’s Con modifier negates the effect for that round).
  • Damage Reduction (Ex): The ooze creature gains DR 5/— (10/— if HD 12+).
  • Engulf (Ex): The ooze gains Improved Overrun, Skirmish, and Throat Punch as bonus feats.
  • Gaseous Form (Ex): The ooze exists as a cloud of smoke or vapor. It loses its Strength score and slam attack, and cannot wear or wield items. However, it gains a Fly speed of 20 ft., damage reduction 10/magic, immunity to poison, and can pass through tiny openings (anything not airtight). For purposes of Fly checks and wind effects, its size is treated as if it were 4 categories smaller than actual (minimum Fine).
  • Immunities (Ex): Select two of the following: acid, bludgeoning damage, cold, electricity, fire, force, negative energy, piercing damage, slashing damage, or sonic. This adaptation can be selected multiple times; each time, choose two more immunities.
  • Natural Armor (Ex): The ooze secretes a shell or hard coating that provides it with a natural armor bonus equal to its ooze creature level, +/-3 per size category above or below Medium.
  • Poison (Ex): The ooze secretes an anesthetizing slime; treat as contact poison; 1d2 Dex/round for 6 rounds, cure 1 save. Some oozes secrete a weakening poison instead (Str damage instead of Dex).
  • Quicksilver (Ex): The ooze flows like liquid mercury; it gains a +10 racial bonus to its Dexterity score (generally increasing it to 11).
  • Split (Ex): Choose two damage types. When the ooze takes damage of that type (or is struck by an attack dealing that type of damage, if immune), it splits into two identical copies of itself (apply damage first, if applicable). Each copy has half the original's remaining hit points (rounded down). An ooze with 10 or fewer hp cannot be further split, and can be killed normally.
  • Suction (Ex): The ooze can create powerful suction against any surface as it climbs, allowing it to cling to inverted surfaces with ease (as the spider climb spell). It can establish or release suction as a swift action; as long as it is using suction, it moves at half speed. Because of the suction, the ooze’s CMD score gets a +10 circumstance bonus to resist bull rush and other attacks and effects that attempt to physically move it from its location.
  • Transparent (Ex): Due to its lack of vivid coloration, the ooze is difficult to discern from its surroundings in most environments. A Perception check (DC 20 + the monster’s Stealth bonus) is required to notice the ooze. Any creature that fails to notice the ooze and walks into it automatically suffers damage as if struck by the ooze's slam attack and is immediately subject to a grab attempt (if applicable) by the ooze.

Weakness (Ex): An ooze can gain a weakness (typical vulnerability to a common energy type). In exchange, it gains one immunity (see above). If an ooze gains fire immunity and vulnerability to cold, it can also gain the [fire] subtype and change its acid to additional fire damage. Other combinations (cold, etc.) are also possible.

Gelatinous Cube

Bits of broken weapons, coins, and a partially digested skeleton are visible inside this quivering cube of slime. Gelatinous cubes are generally 10 feet to a side and weigh upward of 15,000 pounds, though subterranean explorers report larger specimens trawling the deepest caves and corridors.

Gelatinous CubePB Cr 3

Ooze creature 4

N Large ooze

Init –5; Senses blind; blindsight 60 ft.; Perception –5

AC 4, touch 4, flat-footed 4 (-1 size, –5 Dex)

hp 50 (4 HD)

Immune acid, electricity; ooze traits

Fort +9, Ref –4, Int -4, Will –4

Spd 20 ft.

Melee slam +5 (1d6+4 plus 1d8 acid)

Face 10 ft. x 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.

Base Atk +3; CMB +4 (grapple, overrun +6); CMD 9

Special Atks constrict (1d6+4 plus 1d8 acid and DC 14 Fort or can’t speak or breathe), engulf (overrun; 1d6+4 plus 1d8 acid and poison and grab); poison (contact DC 20, 1d2 Dex/round for 6 rds, cure 1 save)

Attributes Str 16, Dex 1, Con 26, Int —, Wis 1, Cha 1

SQ transparent (DC 15)

Feats Improved Grapple, Improved OverrunB, SkirmishB, Throat PunchB, Vital Strike

Skills Stealth (4/-5)

Environment any underground

Frequency uncommon

Organization solitary

Treasure incidental

One of the dungeon's most unusual and specialized predators, gelatinous cubes spend their existence mindlessly roaming dungeon halls and dark caverns, swallowing up organic material such as plants, refuse, carrion, and even living creatures. Materials the cube cannot digest, such as metal and stone, can eventually fill up the creature's mass with such detritus, and at times the creature may excrete some of this material out of its body. Often the treasure and possessions of past victims remain inside the gelatinous cube, leaving a ghostly impression of their material remains.

Sages believe these creatures evolved as a specialized advancement of gray oozes. Some beings use gelatinous cubes as protectors of dungeons and underground fortifications, trapping the immense creatures in massive metal crates and transporting them through either slave power or magic to their final guard posts. They make particularly efficient waste disposals as well—a tribe that can trap a gelatinous cube in a pit or other area that it cannot climb out of can use it as a midden or even a deadly trap, depending only on the ingenuity of the creatures who caught it.

In locations with plentiful sources of food, gelatinous cubes can exist for hundreds of years, if not thousands. However, if denied organic material for more than 6 months, a gelatinous cube begins shrinking. Eventually this stresses its walls and the creature leaks rapidly evaporating slimy liquid until its body collapses and disappears completely.

Gray Ooze

A seemingly mundane puddle, patch of moist stone, or glistening rock is suddenly revealed to be more as a terrible pseudopod lashes out.

Gray OozePB Cr 2

Ooze creature 4

Init –5; Senses blind; blindsight 60 ft.; Perception –5

AC 5, touch 5, flat-footed 5 (–5 Dex)

hp 37 (3 HD)

Attributes Str 15, Dex 1, Con 26, Int —, Wis 1, Cha 1

SQ transparent (DC 19)

Feats Improved Grapple, Vital Strike

Skills Stealth (3/-2)

Environment cold marshes and underground

Frequency rare

Organization solitary

Treasure none

Slinking their way through cold swamps and bleary marshlands, or even dungeons and caverns, gray oozes consume any organic materials they encounter. Despite its lack of intelligence, the gray ooze is a most problematic creature due to its transparency. While the ooze cannot easily climb walls or swim, its habit of lurking in the thick mud that lines the banks of marsh pools or lying in harmless-looking pools on dull-colored dungeon floors makes it dangerously easy to overlook and step on.

Conversion Notes: attribute array: standard; trait: feat mastery (grapple); adaptations: corrosive acid, immunities, transparent.

sections.text:
This towering humanoid figure appears to be sculpted from clay into the form of a stone giant. Fine cracks thread through the body, leaking a stream of putrescent slime. A benaioh in its clay vessel stands just over 12 feet tall and weighs 2,000 pounds.
BenaiohPF93 (Clay Vessel)	Cr 4
Giant, monstrousSS construct 4
N Large construct

(-1 size, -1 Dex, +9 natural)

Spd 20 ft.
Melee slam +11 (1d8+13)
Face 5 ft. x 5 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Base Atk +3; CMB +13; CMD 22

Supernatural Abilities (ML 4th)
3/day—slime spray (4d6 plus disease, DC 21)
Attributes Str 28, Dex 9, Con ―, Int ―, Wis 2, Cha 1
SQ CP 3 (bestial might, death throes, thick hide)
Feats Toughness, Unclean Strike
Skills Perception (4/+0)
Environment any mountains or underground
Frequency rare
Organization solitary or guard (2-12)
Slime Spray (Su) Acid splash (0 level) + Reach Spell (close to medium; +1 level) = 1st level; damage cap 5d6.
Ancient stone giant cultures prepared corpses by decomposing them within a clay vessel that the priests believed would allow the soul to escape. To augment this process, the priests used slender, flesh-devouring worms that were imbued with divine blessings. Over the course of a lengthy ritual, priests sealed the body in sacred clay. As the clay hardened, they sculpted it to resemble the likeness of the deceased, forming a sort of upright, statue-like sarcophagus. Holes that allowed access to the individual’s eyes and mouth; the priests placed three of the sacred worms into each of the vessel’s openings, then sealed the openings with wax.

As a side effect, this strange burial practice provided guardians for the tombs, as the divinely-imbued worms eventually animate their clay vessels as benaiohs. The worms are able to breed rapidly and then maintain a stable population indefinitely; benaiohs are capable of standing vigil for millennia.

At will—blight (DC 18), invisibility, hallucinatory terrain (21 x 20-ft. cubes, DC 20)
Attributes Str 38, Dex 32, Con 32, Int 20, Wis 21, Cha 24

Feats Canny Defense, Crippling Debilitation, Favored Terrain, Improved Critical, Improved GrappleB, Improved Initiative, Improved Sunder, Iron Will, Power Attack, Staggering Strike, Vital Strike
Skills Athletics (21/+35; climb +39), Bluff (21/+28),  Endurance (21/+32), Perception (21/+26), Profession (mining) (21/+30), Stealth (21/+32; +36 underground)
Environment any underground
Frequency very rare
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Irradiate Domain (Sp) Damage attribute (Con; 1st level) + Crippling Drain (+1 level) + Accursed Spell (+1 level) + Shape Spell (target to cubes; +3 levels) + Widen Spell (10-ft. to 20-ft. cubes; +1 level) + Extend Spell (onset: 1/day to 1/10 minutes; +2 levels) + Location-Specific Spell (blight’s domain; -2 levels) = 7th level; those within blight’s domain (up to 21 20-ft. cubes) take 1d4 Con drain every 10 minutes (DC 24 Fort half).

Cave blights are radioactive oozes that dwell in immense networks of caverns deep below the surface of the world. There, they seek to ruin underground societies—especially svirfneblin settlements, for deep gnomes particularly enrage these oozes due to their ancient links to the primal realm of the fey. Cave blights alone among their kind are adept at magically compelling aberrations to aid them in their wars against other intelligent life.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: NPC (+4 Dex, -4 Cha); racial trait: agile climber; evolutions: favored terrain, natural armor, poison, quicksilver. A cave blight’s power is uncontested in its domain, and as a Champion-tier threat, it represents a threat to entire underground civilizations. It is not, however, a virtual demigod (as the Pathfinder CR of 19 would suggest).

Mosquitoes Aura (Sp) Invisible needle (0 level) + Lingering Evocation (+1 level) + Reach Spell (close to touch; -1 level) + Cascade Spell (sickening touch; +1 level) + Augment Spell (nausea; +2 levels) + Extend Spell (nausea: 1 rd./level to 1 rd.; -1 level) + Shape Spell (target to emanation; +2 levels) + Widen Spell (20’r. to 10’r.; -1 level) + Extend Spell (aura: inst. to 1 min./level; +2 levels) = 6th level; damage cap 15d6 piercing plus 1d6 bleed and nauseated 1 rd./level.
Unquiet Bog (Sp) Lesser animate dead (2nd level) + Augment Spell (1d3 at a time; +1 level) + Augment Spell (CR 4; +2 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (bog mummies only; -2 levels) + Shape Spell (target to horizontal wall; +1 level) + Location-Specific Spell (in heart of blight’s swamp; -2 levels) = 2nd level x CL 7th x 1,000 = 14,000 numen. Humanoid creatures that die within five designated 10-ft. squares of the swamp blight’s domain rise from death as bog mummies (up to 1d3 per round).

Swamp blights rule over large swaths of boggy land, populating their realms with the mummified forms of those they have slaughtered or who have fallen prey to their domains’ denizens. These mummies are the swamp blights’ preferred weapon against nearby settlements, and the mummies typically seek to drag the unconscious bodies of their victims back to be killed within their masters’ cursed swamplands so the bodies rise as new mummies to bolster the sodden, undead army. Yet even these undead eventually fall prey to the blights’ unwillingness to share their realms.
Conversion Notes: attribute array: NPC (-2 Int, +2 Cha); racial trait: strong swimmer; evolutions: fast healing, natural armor, poison, quicksilver. A swamp blight’s power is largely uncontested in its domain, and as a Champion-tier threat, it represents a threat to local civilizations. It is not, however, a virtual demigod (as the Pathfinder CR of 17 would suggest).

Unquiet Bog (Sp) Lesser animate dead (2nd level) + Augment Spell (1d3 at a time; +1 level) + Augment Spell (CR 4; +2 levels) + Creature-Specific Spell (bog mummies only; -2 levels) + Shape Spell (target to horizontal wall; +1 level) + Location-Specific Spell (in heart of blight’s swamp; -2 levels) = 2nd level x CL 7th x 1,000 = 14,000 numen. Humanoid creatures that die within five designated 10-ft. squares of the swamp blight’s domain rise from death as bog mummies (up to 1d3 per round).

Swamp blights rule over large swaths of boggy land, populating their realms with the mummified forms of those they have slaughtered or who have fallen prey to their domains’ denizens. These mummies are the swamp blights’ preferred weapon against nearby settlements, and the mummies typically seek to drag the unconscious bodies of their victims back to be killed within their masters’ cursed swamplands so the bodies rise as new mummies to bolster the sodden, undead army. Yet even these undead eventually fall prey to the blights’ unwillingness to share their realms.

Conversion Notes: attribute array: NPC (-2 Int, +2 Cha); racial trait: strong swimmer; evolutions: fast healing, natural armor, poison, quicksilver. A swamp blight’s power is largely uncontested in its domain, and as a Champion-tier threat, it represents a threat to local civilizations. It is not, however, a virtual demigod (as the Pathfinder CR of 17 would suggest).
